newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET MIXED IN QUIET MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET MIXED IN QUIET MARKET.

text.p: Trade on Zimbabwe's money market was low on Thursday morning ahead of a weekly treasury bill tender later in the day, with short-term trading rates quoted stable to weaker, dealers said.
"There isn't much trading at the moment, people are just waiting for the tender," said one.
Earlier in the week, the dealers predicted the benchmark tender rate was likely to soften at the auction on the back of liquidity.

On Thursday morning, discount houses were indicating to sell treasury bills at 17.65 percent, down from 17.80 percent the previous day, while bankers acceptance bills were quoted steady at 18.50 percent (buying) but firmer at 18 percent from 17.75 (selling).
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days eased to 19 percent from 19.50 percent (buying) but were being bought unchanged at 18.25 percent.
Call money was also unmoved from 18.50 percent in a market which had a surplus of Z$212.1 million under Wednesday's date from Z$523.2 million.
